idiom_name: handle struct + pthread_once (or C11 call_once) guard
implementation_notes: C has no lazy-value type, so the stand-in is a struct holding what construction needs (path, key, configuration) plus the real object pointer, and the deferral is a pthread_once guard wrapping the initializer; the forwarding functions call the guard before touching the pointer. C11 <threads.h> call_once/once_flag is the portable ISO equivalent, implemented on top of pthread_once, and C23 also exposes once_flag in <stdlib.h>. This is the classic structure in the literal sense: nothing in the language defers construction, so the guard plus struct is the mechanism, not a workaround, and it is justified whenever the subject is expensive and access may be concurrent.
pitfalls: The once_control must have static storage duration and be initialized with PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT; an automatic once_control is undefined behaviour.
pthread_once is process-wide, not per-object: a per-instance lazy member needs its own guard inside the instance, not a single file-scope flag.
Recursive use of the same once_control inside its own initializer never completes (the recursive call blocks forever), so the initializer must not touch the guarded member.
